deepseek.ladder: V4-Pro is shape-matched to V3.1 at 61 layers, hidden 7168 and 128 query heads, which makes the generation gap readable directly. Flash → Pro moves width, depth, query heads, expert count and retrieval budget and changes no mechanism at all — the compression ratios, window, indexer width, top-k, hash-layer count and residual-lane count are identical.
deepseek.lede: Two generations sit in this family. DeepSeek-V3.1 is Multi-head Latent Attention — compression along the *head* dimension, one 512-dim latent plus a 64-dim decoupled rotary key per token per layer. The two V4 rungs compress along the *sequence* dimension instead: learned gated pooling collapses runs of tokens into single KV entries, a Lightning Indexer selects among them, and an unconditional 128-token uncompressed window restores the local detail compression destroys.

exaone.ladder: This is deliberately not a scale sweep. EXAONE-4.5-33B is EXAONE-4.0's text stack — same 64 layers, same 5120/27392, byte-identical `layer_types` — re-tokenised and given an MTP head and a vision tower, while K-EXAONE is a separate Korean sovereign line: MoE, its own tokenizer, a 128-token window, a commercial licence, and conventional pre-norm where the other two are post-norm.
exaone.lede: All three EXAONE rungs share one attention design: a 3:1 local/global interleave in which RoPE runs only on the sliding-window layers and every global layer carries no positional encoding at all, with per-head RMSNorm on Q and K. What surrounds that design is not shared — norm placement, FFN sparsity, window size, tokenizer and the presence of an MTP head all differ.

gemma-4.ladder: Only 12B → 31B approximates a width-and-depth scale-up, and even that pair diverges on global KV heads. E2B adds per-layer embeddings, cross-layer KV sharing and a double-wide MLP on its shared span; 12B is a different architecture class (`gemma4_unified`) with an encoder-free multimodal front end, added after the family launch.
gemma-4.lede: Gemma 4 is a dense decoder whose defining move is that global and sliding layers are structurally different blocks: the global layers run 512-wide heads against the sliding layers' 256, use a different rotary scheme, and on 12B and 31B carry no `v_proj` at all. Every layer wraps both sub-blocks in Gemma's double RMSNorm, and the softmax has no `1/√d` scale — the temperature is learned into the QK norms.

glm.ladder: Two of these rungs are one architecture at two sizes; the third is a different block. GLM-4.5-Air and GLM-4.7 differ only in depth, width, expert count, `routed_scaling_factor` and QK-norm — every one of which is the Air-versus-full split inside the GLM-4.5 generation — while GLM-4.7-Flash replaces GQA with Multi-head Latent Attention.
glm.lede: GLM's 355B line is a deep, narrow MoE with an unusually wide query side — 96 query heads to 8 KV heads — a one-to-three-layer dense prefix, and DeepSeek-V3's sigmoid router with an aux-loss-free correction bias. Partial rotary at 0.5 is a GLM inheritance: half of every head's dimensions are rotated, half pass through unrotated. All three rungs ship an MTP module that transformers drops at load and that this study never drove.

ministral-3.ladder: Four knobs move: depth, hidden width, FFN width, and the RoPE base, which jumps from 1e6 on the 3B and 8B to 1e9 on the 14B. Because head dim is pinned at 128 while hidden size grows, the attention projection is wider than the residual stream on the 3B, exactly square on the 8B and narrower on the 14B.
ministral-3.lede: Ministral-3 is the plainest family on the page: the same dense SwiGLU block repeated 26, 34 or 40 times, with global causal attention on every layer and no windowing anywhere. The head configuration is byte-identical across the ladder — 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128 — so KV cost scales with depth alone. All the interesting engineering is positional.

nemotron-3.ladder: The channel mixer is the ladder's axis — dense MLP, then MoE, then LatentMoE — but the bottom rung is not a small Nemotron-3 at all: the 4B was pruned and distilled from Nemotron Nano 9B v2, a previous-generation model, which is why hidden size runs 3136 → 2688 → 4096 and the 4B's data cutoff is 18 months older.
nemotron-3.lede: Nemotron-3 is a Mamba-2 / attention hybrid in which each layer carries exactly one mixer — a Mamba-2 block, an attention block, or a channel mixer — rather than the usual attention-plus-FFN pair. Attention is 9 to 12 percent of layers, every attention layer is immediately preceded by a Mamba-2 layer, and there is no rotary embedding anywhere in the family. Channel mixers are ungated squared-ReLU, two matrices instead of SwiGLU's three.

qwen3.5.ladder: The one architectural break is at the bottom: the 27B is dense, both larger rungs are fine-grained MoE with a sigmoid-gated shared expert. Depth, hidden width, expert count and top-k all move — and none of them monotonically, since the dense rung is the deepest and widest of the three.
qwen3.5.lede: Qwen3.5 is a Qwen3-Next-derived hybrid: three Gated DeltaNet layers for every one softmax-attention layer, wrapped in a Qwen3-VL multimodal shell that the study never built. All three rungs share the tile, the head geometry, the rotary scheme, the zero-centred RMSNorms and the 248,320-token tokenizer. No Qwen3.5 technical report exists — every mechanism name here comes from the reference implementations and the papers for each borrowed part.

footer: Built for the SmolBench family-ladder scaling study. Structural data fetched 2026-08-12 from Hugging Face; served-context and tensor-parallel figures from `smolbench/evals/ec2.py`.

Colour categories were validated for colour-vision separation and surface contrast in both light and dark themes. Every coloured cell also carries its meaning in text, so nothing on this page depends on hue alone.
howToRead: Each checkpoint gets two drawings. The **genome strip** shows its whole stack, one cell per layer, so twenty-one models can be compared by scanning down the page. The **block schematic** underneath expands the repeating unit and fills in the numbers.

The strip has two tracks. The upper track is the **token mixer** — the thing that moves information between positions. The lower track is the **feed-forward** — the thing that transforms each position on its own. Colour is the mixer's mechanism; a filled lower cell means that layer routes to experts, an outlined one means an ordinary dense MLP.

Bar height on the mixer track is **attention span**. A full-height bar attends to the entire context; a short bar is windowed, log-scaled by its window size. This is the one place the strip encodes a magnitude instead of a category, and it is what makes K-EXAONE's 128-token window and EXAONE-4.0's 4096-token window read as different things rather than both as "sliding".
method: Every structural number on this page — layer counts, head counts, head dimensions, RoPE bases and scaling parameters, expert counts, window sizes, state sizes, vocabulary sizes — was fetched on 2026-08-12 from the exact Hugging Face repository each lane served, and each record carries that repo's resolved commit SHA. The fetch is reproducible: `scripts/arch/fetch_arch_facts.py`.

The fetched values were cross-checked against `tests/fixtures/roster_configs.json`, the fixture the fleet's own deploy-spec test pins against, on the four fields both hold. All twenty-one agree, so no checkpoint moved under the study between launch and this page.

Prose — what a mechanism is *called*, when a checkpoint was released, how many parameters it has — cannot come from a config file. Those claims come from published model cards, technical reports and reference implementations, cited per model. Where a source contradicts the config, the contradiction is shown rather than smoothed over; those are the dashed flags.
position: Ask twenty-one 2026 checkpoints how they encode position and you get one answer, arrived at seven different ways: **less than they used to**. Rotary position embedding was originally applied to every dimension of every attention head. On this roster it reaches a quarter of a head in Qwen3.5 and in Gemma-4's global layers, half in GLM-4.5-Air and GLM-4.7, a third in DeepSeek-V3.1, an eighth in DeepSeek-V4 — and, in two whole families, nothing at all on the layers that see the entire context.

Three of the twenty-one still rotate a complete head: the three Ministral-3 rungs. They are also the only three checkpoints here with no windowed layers, no recurrent mixer and no expert routing. The plainest architecture on the page is the last one still encoding position the plain way.
positionNotes: **Unrotated is not the same as order-blind.** A head with no rotary encoding still knows about order: the causal mask, the short depthwise convolution in front of every gated-linear and Mamba-2 block, and the recurrence itself all carry position. What this chart measures is how much of the *explicit* positional signal each attention head is handed — not whether the model has a sense of sequence.

**Two superficially similar configs are different mechanisms.** Qwen3.5's `partial_rotary_factor: 0.25` is the GPT-NeoX scheme — rotate the first quarter of the dimensions, leave the rest alone. Gemma-4's `rope_type: "proportional"` is p-RoPE, which computes its frequencies against the *full* head width and so truncates the lowest frequencies rather than subsampling the spectrum. Both read as "25%"; they do different things to the low-frequency end.

**And two families declare rotary parameters that nothing reads.** Nemotron-3's two larger rungs ship `rope_theta` and `partial_rotary_factor` in their configs; the reference implementation passes no positions into attention at all. Those rungs are charted at what the code does, not what the config says — the discrepancy is flagged on each model.
readNotes: **Where a track is empty, nothing is missing.** Nemotron-3 is the only family here whose layers are *either* a mixer *or* a feed-forward, never both — so its two tracks interleave rather than stack. Every other family puts a mixer and an FFN in every layer. The gaps are the architecture, not a gap in the data.

**The residual stream is not drawn.** Fourteen of the twenty-one wrap every sub-block in the plain pre-norm residual, `x + Op(Norm(x))`; drawing that fourteen times would add no information. The seven that do something else all say so in their own schematic caption — the two EXAONE-4.x rungs normalise *after* each sub-block, the three Gemma-4 rungs use a double norm on both sides of every sub-block, and the two DeepSeek-V4 rungs do not have a single residual stream at all: they carry four parallel lanes, remixed at every junction.
**Layer counts, not parameter counts, set the drawing.** A 92-layer stack is drawn as tall as it is because that is what the config says; expert counts and widths live in the schematic's labels.

**Two of the twenty-one never completed a serve.** The DeepSeek-V4 rungs are described here from their weights and configs like everything else, and carry a badge saying so — they are part of the roster the study was designed around, so dropping them would misdescribe the study.
intro.standfirst: Twenty-one open-weight checkpoints — seven families, three size rungs each — make up the roster of the SmolBench family-ladder study. This is what is actually inside them: how every layer mixes tokens, how every layer encodes position, and where the feed-forward goes sparse. Every structural number here is read from the checkpoint's own `config.json`.

note.attention:
`num_key_value_heads: 128` is vestigial: MLA replaces grouped-query sharing entirely. The query path is 7168 → 1536 → RMSNorm → 128 heads × 192, split 128 nope plus 64 rope. The KV path is 7168 → 512 latent plus a 64-dimensional rotary key, and only those 576 elements are stored; per-head keys and values are reconstructed after the cache read and never cached themselves.

Head dimensions are asymmetric and worth drawing: Q and K are 192-dimensional while V is 128. `attention_bias: false`, no dropout, no window.
extras: Weights ship FP8 e4m3 with `weight_block_size: [128, 128]` and, notably, `scale_fmt: "ue8m0"` — an 8-bit unsigned-exponent, zero-mantissa scale, so applying it is an exponent add and is mantissa-lossless. The card names the motive: compatibility with microscaling formats.
RMSNorm at eps 1e-6, pre-norm, plus the two extra RMSNorms inside MLA on the query latent and the KV latent.

The one-layer MTP module consumes the trunk's hidden state for token *t* with the embedding of token *t+1* and predicts *t+2*, sharing the embedding matrix and output head. No `--speculative-config` was passed.
Served with BF16 KV — no `--kv-cache-dtype` — which is why the per-token figure here is ~69 KB rather than the ~34 KB the same 576 elements would cost in V4's FP8 slot layout.
note.ffn:
Layers 0 through 2 are dense SwiGLU at width 18432; layers 3 through 60 are sparse — 256 routed experts of width 2048, top-8, plus one shared expert. Affinity is a sigmoid over the token-centroid product rather than a softmax over experts; the eight selected gates are renormalised to sum to one and the routed contribution is then scaled by 2.5 before the shared expert is added.

Balancing is aux-loss-free: a per-expert learnable bias is added to the affinity for top-k selection only and never to the gate value used for weighting, so load balance costs no interference gradient in the language-model objective. The card additionally requires that bias be loaded and computed in fp32.

Routing is node-limited: `n_group: 8` and `topk_group: 4` partition the 256 experts into 8 groups, a token first picks its top-4 groups, then draws its 8 experts only from those. With one group per node in expert parallelism, a token's activations reach at most four nodes.

flags.text: The HF repo advertises 685B against the card's 671B. The ~14 B delta is the MTP module, which the card's figure excludes — the same trunk-only counting convention seen elsewhere on this page.

Context: the config permits 163,840, the vendor advertises 128K, and the study served 131,072. The architecture is one YaRN configuration spanning 4K to 163,840; the model was trained into it in two data phases (630 B tokens at 32K, then 209 B at 128K), and the advertised figure is the one actually trained.

note.pe:
Rotary applies only to the 64-dimensional `qk_rope_head_dim` slice. The 128-dimensional nope slice and the entire 128-dimensional value head are not rotated. YaRN then carries the window: `factor: 40` over `original_max_position_embeddings: 4096` gives exactly 163,840, so the scaling factor is what *defines* the declared window rather than stretching a pre-existing one.

YaRN here is NTK-by-parts — dimensions whose wavelength exceeds the original window are position-interpolated, high-frequency dimensions are left untouched, and a linear ramp covers the middle. `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` are both pinned to 1.0, which disables YaRN's attention-logit temperature correction. Treatment is uniform across all 61 layers.

The reason only 64 dimensions rotate is mechanical. MLA's efficiency depends on absorbing the key up-projection into the query at inference; rotary does not commute with that absorption, so DeepSeek carves out a separate 64-dimensional key that carries all the positional information, shares it MQA-style across all 128 query heads, and caches it next to the latent. The cost of full-rank positional encoding is 64 of 576 elements — 11% cache overhead.
note.signature: Multi-head Latent Attention: 128 query heads score against a single 512-dimensional latent plus a 64-dimensional decoupled rotary key, and those 576 elements per layer are the only thing ever written to cache — a 57× reduction against the equivalent multi-head attention.

note.attention:
Not MLA. `kv_lora_rank`, `qk_nope_head_dim` and `v_head_dim` are gone from the config; there is no key or value up-projection left to absorb. Instead: one 512-dimensional KV row per token serves all 64 query heads, and the same tensor is read as key and as value. Queries stay low-rank — 4096 → 1024 → RMSNorm → 64 × 512 — and that post-norm latent is reused as the indexer's input.

Sequence compression is learned gated pooling, not strided subsampling: two projections give content and compression weights, every *m* consecutive entries collapse into one via a softmax over the window plus a learnable per-slot positional bias. At the 4:1 ratio the windows **overlap** — each compressed entry is a weighted sum of 8 source tokens at stride 4 — while the 128:1 pooling is non-overlapping.

That gives three layer kinds. Sliding-only layers see 128 recent tokens and nothing else. CSA layers pool 4:1 and use the Lightning Indexer to select the top 512 compressed entries, roughly 2048 source tokens of long-range reach. HCA layers pool 128:1 and attend all compressed entries densely, with no indexer at all. The 128-token uncompressed window is additive on **every** layer, concatenated onto the selected entries in a single sparse-attention call.
extras: The routed experts are stored in FP4 (`float4_e2m1fn_x2` with an FP8 block scale) while the shared expert and the whole trunk stay FP8 e4m3 with UE8M0 scales — mixed precision inside one checkpoint.

The output projection is grouped and low-rank: 64 heads split into 8 groups of 8, each projected 4096 → 1024, then the concatenated 8×1024 projected to hidden. About 67 M parameters against 134 M dense.

Three mechanisms have no config field at all and must be read from the paper: per-head learnable attention-sink logits added to the softmax denominator, an extra RMSNorm on each query head and on the compressed KV head before core attention, and the inverse rotary on the output.
`compress_ratios` carries 44 entries for 43 layers — the trailing entry is the MTP module, and it is `0`, so the MTP layer is sliding-window-only.

The repo ships no Jinja chat template; the protocol lives in a Python module with a DSML tool-call dialect and three reasoning modes, of which "max" is a literal prepended system paragraph rather than a sampling setting. The study supplied an inline template.
note.ffn:
There is no dense FFN anywhere — no `intermediate_size`, no `first_k_dense_replace`, no `moe_layer_freq`. All 43 layers are MoE at 256 routed experts of width 2048, top-6, plus one shared expert.

What replaced the dense prefix is `num_hash_layers: 3`: the first three MoE layers select their experts from a **frozen token-ID lookup table** rather than a learned router. Selection is pure token identity — perfectly balanced by construction, zero router parameters, no correction bias — while the mixing weights still come from the learned affinity score. Beyond those three, routing scores are `√(softplus(x))`, replacing V3's sigmoid; unlike sigmoid it is unbounded above, so a strongly-matched expert is not saturated toward 1.0. The activation is SwiGLU with its pre-activations clamped at 10.0 — two-sided on the up projection, upper-only on the gate.

note.pe:
Positional treatment is not uniform across layers, which is unusual on this page. The main stream uses `rope_theta: 10000` applied to the **last 64 of 512** dimensions of every query vector and of the single KV entry — the paper says so literally and the reference implementation matches. The other 448 dimensions are unrotated.

A second base, `compress_rope_theta: 160000`, is applied to the compressed KV stream and to the indexer on every layer that has a compressor. Layers with no compressor — the two sliding-only layers here — disable YaRN entirely and fall back to the plain base, under a comment reading "disable YaRN and use base rope_theta in pure sliding-window attention". YaRN itself is `factor: 16` over `original_max_position_embeddings: 65536`, giving exactly the declared 1,048,576.

Rotary appears **twice** in the block. Because V4 reads the same tensor as both key and value, the value picks up the key's rotation, so the attention output's trailing 64 dimensions are counter-rotated at the query position — the conjugate rotation, undoing it. The net effect is that each entry's contribution depends only on its relative distance to the query.

note.attention:
The same hybrid as Flash at twice the query heads. One 512-dimensional KV row per token serves all 128 query heads and is read as both key and value; the query path is 7168 → 1536 → RMSNorm → 128 × 512. CSA layers pool 4:1 with overlapping windows and select the top **1024** compressed entries — roughly 4096 source tokens of long-range reach, twice Flash's — while HCA layers pool 128:1 and attend all compressed entries densely. The 128-token uncompressed window is unconditional and additive on every layer.

The retrieval *budget* scales with model size; the indexer's *width* does not — `index_n_heads: 64` and `index_head_dim: 128` are identical to Flash's. The output projection is grouped low-rank at `o_groups: 16` and rank 1024, which at 128 heads is 8 heads per group — exactly Flash's group width, so `o_groups` tracks head count rather than signalling a design change.
extras: Routed experts are FP4; the shared expert and the trunk are FP8 e4m3 with UE8M0 scales.

`compress_ratios` reads `[128, 128, 4, 128, 4, …, 4, 0]` — 62 entries for 61 layers, the last being the MTP module. Pro has **no** sliding-only layers: its first two are HCA where Flash's first two see only 128 local tokens. The reason is unverified.
Per-head learnable attention-sink logits, per-head Q and KV RMSNorms before core attention, and the inverse rotary on the output have no config field at all and come from the paper.

mHC is the residual stream, not a clustering component: the embedding is expanded to four lanes, every layer wraps its attention and its FFN in a mix-down/mix-up pair, and the 4×4 mixing matrix is projected onto the doubly stochastic matrices by Sinkhorn-Knopp with `hc_eps: 1e-6` as the floor.
Weights measured at 865 GB. No Jinja chat template ships; the study supplied an inline one.
note.ffn:
All 61 layers are MoE — no dense FFN and no `first_k_dense_replace`. Three hundred and eighty-four routed experts of width 3072, top-6, plus one shared expert: scale is bought with more and wider experts at a constant activation count. The first three layers are hash-routed from a frozen token-ID table rather than a learned router. Scores are `√(softplus(x))`, the selected six are renormalised, and the routed branch is scaled by 2.5 — where Flash uses 1.5, for reasons no source states.

Activation is SwiGLU with pre-activations clamped at 10.0, two-sided on the up projection and upper-only on the gate, bounding magnitude for the FP4 expert path.

The earlier closure — that vLLM raises `NotImplementedError("DeepGEMM MegaMoE requires SM100 GPUs.")` — was itself refuted: that raise sits behind an opt-in `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` the study never passed, an in-tree SM90 serving path is now pinned in `smolbench/evals/ec2.py`, and as of 2026-08-12 the actual construction-time crash cause remains undiagnosed.

vLLM and DeepSeek's reference disagree about how the MTP block reads `compress_ratios`: DeepSeek indexes the trailing entry, vLLM comments that the MTP layer is not in the list and hardcodes 1. Numerically harmless — both land on sliding-only — but note the polarity flip, since in vLLM a ratio of 1 means "no compressor" while in DeepSeek's code 0 does.

Three V4 design choices have no published rationale: why node-limited routing was dropped (`n_group`/`topk_group` are gone and the gate does a flat top-6), why the routing score became √softplus, and why `routed_scaling_factor` differs between the two V4 rungs. No ablation is published, and the V4 report is an explicit preview with no hyperparameter table.

note.attention:
Grouped-query attention, 40 query heads to 8 KV heads, `head_dim: 128` — and here `40 × 128 = 5120` is exactly the hidden size, so the query and output projections are square. Per-head RMSNorm on Q and K, over the head dim rather than the full projection, applied after reshape and before rotary. No attention bias — the checkpoint contains no `self_attn.*.bias` tensors.

The interleave is `sliding_window_pattern: "LLLG"` — three sliding layers with a 4096-token window, then one global layer, sixteen times, ending on a global layer. Because the sliding layers' cache is capped by the window, the global layers carry the growth: 16 × 4 KiB per token reaches 8.0 GiB across a 131,072-token sequence, while all 48 sliding layers together hold a flat 0.75 GiB. That is roughly a 3.7× reduction against an all-global stack of the same depth.
extras: Because rotary only ever runs on a 4096-token windowed layer, the largest relative offset any rotary dot product sees is the window — not the context length. On that reading the llama3 scaling is a leftover of the staged 4K → 32K → 128K context-extension recipe rather than a load-bearing long-context mechanism.

p-RoPE is frequency *truncation*, not interpolation. Because the config injects a per-layer `head_dim: 512` override on full-attention layers before rotary init, `partial_rotary_factor: 0.25` rotates 128 of 512 dimensions and leaves 384 as pure NoPE channels. Those dimensions are not sliced out — their `inv_freq` entries are zero-padded, so `cos = 1`, `sin = 0` and the rotation is an algebraic identity.

Dropping llama3 scaling is not a regression, it is the design admitting the scaling was never doing the work. Rotary's dot product depends only on relative offset, and here rotary exists only on layers whose mask caps that offset at 128 tokens. No frequency in the model is ever evaluated at an offset it was not trained on, however long the context; length generalisation is carried entirely by the position-blind global layers.

note.pe:
Three long-context mechanisms stacked on one another. The base is 1e6, which puts 27 of 64 frequency pairs beyond a full rotation inside the 16,384-token pre-extension window — they act as slow positional-magnitude channels rather than oscillators. Third, `llama_4_scaling_beta: 0.1` is Llama 4's position-dependent query temperature — the query vector multiplied by `1 + 0.1·ln(1 + ⌊pos / 16384⌋)`. note.signature: The same 3:1 recurrence-to-attention tile as the 27B, with every feed-forward slot replaced by 256 fine-grained experts plus one sigmoid-gated shared expert — and a much more aggressive 16:1 grouped-query ratio on the attention layers.

sources.label: Yang, Kautz & Hatamizadeh — Gated Delta Networks (ICLR 2025)

note.attention:
The 16 full-attention layers are grouped-query attention with two additions. Per-head RMSNorm is applied to Q and K before rotary, and `q_proj` is double-width — its second half is a per-head, per-dimension sigmoid gate multiplied elementwise into the SDPA output immediately before `o_proj`. That is the whole of `attn_output_gate`. No sliding window, no softcapping, no attention bias.

The 48 linear layers are Gated DeltaNet: Mamba-2's scalar decay composed with DeltaNet's Householder erase-then-write, giving a matrix-valued state of 128×128 per value head that is constant in sequence length. Sixteen query/key heads are broadcast three-fold to meet 48 value heads — grouped-query sharing inside a recurrent layer. These layers hold no KV cache, so the 16 full-attention layers charge the entire 64 KiB/token figure.
extras: RMSNorm is zero-centred, Gemma-style: weights initialise to zero and the forward is `output * (1.0 + weight)`, in fp32.
A second, conventional gated RMSNorm sits inside each DeltaNet block, normalising then multiplying by `silu(z)` before the output projection.
Untied embeddings: 2 × 5120 × 248320 ≈ 2.54 B parameters in the embedding and LM head alone.
The 1-layer MTP module ships in the checkpoint. transformers discards it at load; vLLM implements it for speculative decoding, which this study did not enable.
`mlp_only_layers: []` and `deepstack_visual_indexes: []` ship in configs whose loader deletes both fields — inherited Qwen2-MoE and Qwen3-VL cruft.
note.ffn: Every one of the 64 layers carries the same dense SwiGLU MLP at `intermediate_size: 17408`. The config declares no `num_experts`, no `moe_intermediate_size` and no shared-expert width, and the dense text-config class declares every MoE attribute an `AttributeError` — this rung is dense by construction, not by a disabled switch.

flags.text: The model card's 1,010,000-token context is an opt-in user edit — a YaRN block with `factor: 4.0` the README tells you to paste in. The shipped config declares `rope_type: "default"` and no scaling of any kind. A research pass that reported the shipped config as YaRN was wrong; a direct raw fetch confirms otherwise.

`attn_output_gate: true` is read by vLLM, which sizes `qkv` as `num_heads * (1 + attn_output_gate)`, and ignored by transformers, where the double-width `q_proj` and the sigmoid multiply are unconditional. Both agree on this checkpoint because the value is `true`, but a `false` config would be honoured by one reader and silently dropped by the other.

No Qwen3.5 technical report could be found on arXiv as of 2026-08-12, and the official blog is a JS-rendered page that could not be read. Every architecture claim here rests on the config, the two reference implementations, the model cards, and the papers for each borrowed mechanism.

note.pe:
Rotary reaches 25% of the dimensions of 25% of the layers. `partial_rotary_factor: 0.25` over `head_dim: 256` rotates 64 dims — 32 frequency pairs at base 1e7 — and concatenates the untouched 192 back unchanged, so those channels compare on content alone. The other 48 layers are Gated DeltaNet and receive no `position_ids` at all: their forward signature does not accept them. Position there is carried by the 4-tap causal depthwise convolution and by the strictly sequential state update, whose decay makes the state a recency-weighted summary.

The config's M-RoPE fields — `mrope_interleaved: true`, `mrope_section: [11, 11, 10]`, summing exactly to the 32 frequency pairs — belong to the Qwen3-VL shell. For text-only input M-RoPE degenerates to ordinary 1-D partial RoPE, and vLLM strips the fields outright when serving text; under `--language-model-only` they were inert for this study. There is no RoPE scaling: `rope_type` is `default` and the config contains no `rope_scaling` key anywhere.

note.attention:
Fifteen full-attention layers at 32 query heads to 2 KV heads, `head_dim: 256`, QK-norm before rotary, sigmoid output gate. The attention runs 8192 dimensions wide against hidden 4096 — twice the residual stream.

Forty-five Gated DeltaNet layers, 16 query/key heads broadcast four-fold onto 64 value heads, 128×128 state, 4-tap causal convolution. The FP8 exclusion list confirms the tiling independently: it names a `linear_attn` submodule for every layer index except 3, 7, 11, …, 59.
extras: FP8 is `quant_method: "fp8"` with `weight_block_size: [128, 128]` and dynamic activation scaling — fine-grained block FP8, not per-tensor.
Kept in BF16: `lm_head`, `embed_tokens`, every `mlp.gate` and `shared_expert_gate`, every DeltaNet `conv1d` / `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b`, the whole vision tower, and `mtp.fc`.
That exclusion set is coherent — the two DeltaNet gate projections are only 64 channels wide and feed an exponential, and the routers are argmax-sensitive maps into 512 logits.
The 1-layer MTP module ships in the checkpoint and was never driven; no `--speculative-config` was passed.
note.ffn: All 60 layers sparse: 512 routed experts at hidden width 1024, top-10 per token, plus one shared expert of the same width added through a scalar sigmoid gate. Router logits are softmaxed over all 512, top-k selected, then renormalised. `router_aux_loss_coef` is 0.001 and acts in training only.

flags.text: The vendor's parameter headline counts the trunk only. Config-only reconstruction gives 396.3 B against a stated 397 B; adding the 1-layer MTP head — which contains a full MoE block, roughly 6.5 B parameters here — would overshoot the headline on every rung.

vLLM re-fuses this checkpoint's split DeltaNet projections at load time through a `WeightsMapper`, so vLLM-side tensor names (`in_proj_qkvz`, `in_proj_ba`) do not match the FP8 scale names in the checkpoint. Worth knowing before inspecting quantisation metadata.
